structure: Part 6 read eight rows of backlog.json increments[] in full, in file order: inc-058 (lines 8133-8311), inc-057 (8839-9095), inc-056 (17244-17454), inc-052 (17455-17632), inc-045 (17633-17843), inc-063 (18068-18418), inc-047 (22182-22404) and inc-048 (22405-22665). Every row has status "blocked" and decision.ruling "block"; none carries notes, openQuestions or failure_reason. Rows inc-058, inc-057, inc-056, inc-052, inc-045 and inc-063 (domain addresses) were blocked by Rhys on 2026-09-04 because live address work in the consignment party space would collide; inc-047 (domain contact) and inc-048 (domain addresses), both banded needs-backend, were blocked by Rhys on 2026-08-28 pending a typed address-book record that travels with the address book to trade-imports-ins-frontend, a note that also calls them deferred. Each row is laid out as id, type, domain, title, detail (frontend, prototype, difference and FALSIFIED BY paragraphs), screens, evidence, band, status, finding (frontend, prototype, difference, correction, falsifiedBy, verification, sometimes relatedTo), citations, controls, provenance (sourceA/sourceC, note, better) and decision (ruling, note). Claims record, per row: the ruling, who and when, the reason in decision.note; the difference DR1 judged (what Design release 1 does that the frontend does not, and the change the row prescribes); the corrections, constraints and related-row links its finding records. Citations, screens, evidence and the run-matching provenance notes were read for context and not claimed. Within scope the source is a DR1 judgement record, so claims state what the row records, not requirements of their own.

claims.statement: Row inc-058 (permanent address typed in full; Design release 1 lets the trader reuse the place of destination address) has status blocked and decision.ruling block.
claims.ref: increments[] row inc-058, status and decision.ruling
claims.quote: "ruling": "block"

claims.quote: Blocked by Rhys, 2026-09-04: address work is being done in this space now, so parity changes against it would collide. claims.statement: inc-058 records that the frontend shows a bare "Permanent address" heading and nine empty, ungated address fields on the animal identification card for any animal whose commodity requires a permanent address, with no choice to reuse an address already given.
claims.quote: On the animal identification page, any animal whose commodity requires a permanent address gets a bare "Permanent address" heading followed by nine empty fields, all of them visible at once. There is no choice to make and nothing to reuse
claims.note: finding.correction says the block is gated on card.showAddress (not unconditional); the fields inside it are ungated.

claims.statement: inc-058 records that Design release 1 asks "Where will their permanent address be?" with a two-option radio, "Select an address": "Same as the place of destination (POD)" or "Enter a new address", the second opening the address fields as a conditional reveal.
claims.quote: Design release 1 asks "Where will their permanent address be?" and offers each animal a two-option radio, "Select an address": "Same as the place of destination (POD)", or "Enter a new address", which opens the address fields as a conditional reveal

claims.statement: inc-058 records that the "Enter a new address" option carries the hint "This is where they will stay after spending 48 hours at the place of destination.", unconditionally.
claims.ref: increments[] row inc-058, finding.prototype and finding.correction
claims.quote: What is unconditional, and what the finding had left out, is the hint on the second option, "This is where they will stay after spending 48 hours at the place of destination."

claims.statement: inc-058 records that the "Same as the place of destination (POD)" option shows the place of destination address as its hint only when a place of destination has already been given.
claims.quote: That hint is conditional: app/routes.js:2488-2492 attaches it only when the session already holds a place-of-destination address

claims.statement: The change inc-058 prescribes: add a two-option radio (reuse the place of destination address, or enter a new one) above the permanent address fields, hide the fields behind the second option, and show the chosen destination address as the first option's hint; it needs nothing outside the frontend.
claims.quote: Add a two-option radio above the permanent address fields on the animal identification card — reuse the place of destination address, or enter a new one — and hide the address fields behind the second option. The frontend already collects a place of destination as one of its five consignment parties

claims.statement: inc-058 says it must be read together with inc-057: the radio on the identification card is the smaller standalone change, but once the permanent-address page exists the choice belongs on that page.
claims.ref: increments[] row inc-058, finding.difference and provenance.note
claims.quote: Adding the radio to the card is the smaller, standalone change; once the page exists the choice belongs on it.

claims.ref: increments[] row inc-057, status, decision.ruling and decision.note
claims.quote: Blocked by Rhys, 2026-09-04: address work is being done in this space now, so parity changes against it would collide.

claims.statement: inc-057 records that Design release 1 gives the permanent address its own page, captioned "Consignment parties" and headed "Permanent address", reached from the parties list and back-linked to it.
claims.quote: Design release 1 gives the question a page of its own, captioned "Consignment parties" and headed "Permanent address", reached from the parties list and back-linked to it

claims.statement: inc-057 records that in Design release 1 the permanent address is a consignment address section for commodity code 01061900 (cat, dog, ferret and other live mammals), alongside place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination, answered once for every animal on that line; the frontend asks it for cats and dogs alone.
claims.ref: increments[] row inc-057, finding.prototype and finding.frontend
claims.quote: That commodity code is the whole 01061900 group — cat, dog, ferret and other live mammals — not cats and dogs alone.

claims.statement: inc-057 records that the parties list's "Add a permanent address" link goes to /permanent-address, which clears any previous same-as-destination answer and redirects to /permanent-address/select; the "Are all the animals going to the place of destination?" view is dead code.
claims.ref: increments[] row inc-057, finding.prototype, finding.correction and finding.verification
claims.quote: It is also one page rather than two: /permanent-address writes no to the same-as-destination answer and redirects straight to the select page (app/routes.js:10789-10801), and the sibling view asking whether all the animals are going to the place of destination is dead code

claims.statement: The change inc-057 prescribes: move the permanent address out of the identification card onto its own page in the addresses section, listing every animal that needs one, so a trader can answer it, leave it and come back; no model change is needed because the obligation is already per animal.
claims.quote: Move the permanent address out of the identification card and give it its own page in the addresses section, listing every animal that needs one, so a trader can answer it, leave it and come back.

claims.statement: inc-057 orders the work: the page lands before the same-as-destination choice and the guidance copy; the 01061900-group applicability waits on the frontend commodity catalogue growing past its five entries.
claims.quote: Land this before the same-as-destination choice and the guidance copy, because both of those belong on the page this creates. The applicability difference rides with the commodity catalogue rather than with this page

claims.quote: "ruling": "block"

claims.quote: When a consignee has been chosen, the Importer and Place of destination rows each gain a "Same as consignee" control; when a place of origin has been chosen, the Consignor row gains "Same as place of origin"

claims.quote: Pressing it fills that row in place, from the same page, with no picker in between; the row then shows the copied address and a "Change" link like any other.

claims.statement: The change inc-056 prescribes: show each copy action only when the source party has been answered and the target has not, submitting the hub's own form rather than navigating.
claims.quote: each shown only when the source party has been answered and the target has not. It submits the hub's own form rather than navigating, so the trader stays on the page.

claims.statement: inc-056 records that copying the place of origin onto the consignor must copy the record, not the reference, because place of origin is stored inline while the other parties are stored as references.
claims.quote: Note that place of origin is stored inline while consignor, consignee, importer and destination are stored as references (`inline: true` at :26), so copying the place of origin onto the consignor must copy the record, not the reference.

claims.quote: the Importer row reads "This is usually the same as the consignee. You can select a different person if needed." — and then offers no way to say "the same".

claims.quote: so a copy button in a row cannot post that form as things stand and the rows have to move inside it (or the buttons carry a form attribute).

claims.quote: Show the selected address, not just the name, in every answered row of the Consignment addresses page: name, then the address lines, then postcode and country.

claims.quote: Frontend's fraud warning ends with a full stop — "Providing a false address is an act of fraud." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:4) — and Design release 1's does not

claims.ref: increments[] row inc-047, status, band and decision.ruling

claims.ref: increments[] rows inc-047 and inc-048, decision.note
claims.quote: Blocked by Rhys, 2026-08-28: both are real defects on journey pages the animals frontend keeps, and both findings argue they survive the inc-062 descope. Neither is buildable until an address-book record carries a type, and that record shape travels with the address book to trade-imports-ins-frontend and its own epic. travels-with inc-062. Deferred pending that epic — revisit when the typed record lands.

claims.statement: inc-047 records that Design release 1's contact-address list is a separate collection of the organisation's branch addresses (three, all in Great Britain: Aberdeen, Bristol, Cardiff), not the consignment address book the pickers use.
claims.quote: DR1 draws this list from a separate collection of branch addresses, not from the consignment address book the pickers use

claims.statement: inc-047 records that Design release 1's contact page says the list is for the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain, and its help line tells the trader to "add a new branch address".
claims.quote: The page says what the list is for — the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain — and the help line names the collection when it tells the trader where a missing one comes from: "add a new branch address"

claims.statement: inc-047 records that the frontend contact page offers every record in the organisation's address book (thirteen radios, including overseas records), with nothing to narrow it by.
claims.quote: The contact page offers `addressBook.all(orgId)` — every record in the organisation's book, in book order

claims.statement: The change inc-047 prescribes: narrow the contact list to the trader's own branch addresses, which first needs the address-book API and record shape to distinguish a branch record (DR1's Branch Address type).
claims.quote: Narrow the contact list to the trader's own branch addresses. That needs the address book to distinguish a branch record from a party record — DR1's Branch Address type — which today it deliberately does not, so the API and the record shape have to change before the page can.

claims.statement: inc-047 travels with inc-046 (the sentence DR1 opens the contact page with) and is adjacent to inc-053 (the contact help line's add path); what the page says the contact is for is a separate copy change.
claims.ref: increments[] row inc-047, finding.relatedTo and finding.difference
claims.quote: the sentence DR1 opens the page with is what tells the trader why the list is narrow

claims.statement: Row inc-048 (whole address book on all six pickers) has status blocked, decision.ruling block and band needs-backend, under the same Rhys 2026-08-28 note as inc-047.
claims.ref: increments[] row inc-048, status, band and decision
claims.quote: "band": "needs-backend"

claims.statement: inc-048 records that Design release 1 types every saved address and filters each picker to its type: place of origin offers nine, consignor nine, consignee six, importer six, place of destination three.
claims.quote: Design release 1 types every saved address and filters each picker to its type. Place of origin offers nine foreign farms, consignor nine, consignee six Great Britain importers, importer six, place of destination three

claims.statement: inc-048 records Design release 1's address types: saving an address asks "What is the new address for?" over Place of Origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of Destination, Transporter and, after a divider, Branch Address.
claims.quote: saving an address begins by asking "What is the new address for?" over Place of Origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of Destination, Transporter and, after a divider, Branch Address

claims.statement: inc-048 records that all five frontend party pickers and the contact page show the same undifferentiated list ("Showing 5 of 13 addresses"), because the address-book service carries no type and exposes no role-aware call.
claims.quote: All five party pickers and the contact-address page draw from one undifferentiated list. Every captured picker reports "Showing 5 of 13 addresses"

claims.statement: The change inc-048 prescribes: give a saved address one or more roles and filter each picker by its role, the contact page asking only for a branch address; the address-book API (Standard Address Block records in trade-imports-address-book) must carry the type first and whichever service writes those records must collect it.
claims.quote: Give a saved address one or more roles and filter each picker by the role it is asking for, including the contact page, which asks only for a branch address. The frontend cannot do this alone

claims.statement: inc-048 rules out a partial ship before the type exists: filtering on a guess, such as matching country against direction of travel, would hide addresses the trader legitimately wants.
claims.quote: Until the type exists, no useful half of this can ship: filtering on a guess, such as matching the country against the direction of travel, would hide addresses the trader legitimately wants.

claims.statement: inc-048 says the role type is decided together with the address-book scope question (address-book--saved-address-book-pages-absent, inc-062), because the type is collected on the add form; it is a live defect whichever way that scope is settled.
claims.ref: increments[] row inc-048, finding.difference and finding.relatedTo
claims.quote: Decide it together with the address-book scope question raised as address-book--saved-address-book-pages-absent, because the type is collected on the add form that question is about.

claims.statement: inc-048 absorbed the finding address-book--picker-lists-every-saved-address-regardless-of-role in a pre-ingest merge; they are one change.
claims.quote: The corpus editor merged addresses--picker-lists-every-saved-address-regardless-of-role into this finding before the first ingest and deleted that file

claims.statement: None of the eight rows records a decision on the Design release 1 difference itself (accept or reject); each block defers the work for collision or dependency reasons, so whether Design release 1's design should be adopted once unblocked is not settled by this source.
claims.ref: increments[] rows inc-058, inc-057, inc-056, inc-052, inc-045, inc-063, inc-047, inc-048, decision
claims.note: All decision.note texts give blocking reasons (live address work; typed address-book record pending); none rejects the prototype behaviour. provenance.judged is null on every row.

claims.statement: inc-047 and inc-048 carry status blocked and decision.ruling block, yet the same decision.note ends by calling them deferred pending the address-book epic, so the row's status and its note use two different words for the one judgement.
claims.ref: increments[] rows inc-047 and inc-048, status, decision.ruling and decision.note
claims.quote: Deferred pending that epic — revisit when the typed record lands.
claims.note: Recorded as an ambiguity, not settled: status is "blocked" and ruling "block", while the note says "Deferred". inc-047 is filed under domain "contact"; inc-048 under "addresses".

claims.statement: inc-048's correction records that the frontend's party table already carries a role per party (placeOfOrigin, consignor, consignee, importer, destination) and the picker deliberately ignores it, so what is missing is a type on the address record, not a role on the page.
claims.quote: So the missing half really is the type on the record rather than the role on the page, which is what puts this behind the address-book contract.

claims.statement: inc-063's correction records that, apart from the fraud warning's full stop and the CPH row's capitalisation (owned by the row addresses--cph-wording), every heading and hint on the frontend and Design release 1 Consignment addresses pages matches word for word.
claims.quote: Apart from that and the CPH row's capitalisation, which addresses--cph-wording owns, every heading and hint on the two pages matches word for word.

claims.statement: inc-057 records that the frontend has no permanent address page: the nine address fields are printed inside the animal identification card, between the identifier fields and the "Save and add another" button, and the only way back to them is to reopen animal identification.
claims.quote: The frontend has no permanent address page. For a commodity that needs one, the nine address fields are printed inside the animal identification card, between the identifier fields and the "Save and add another" button
